definitions.explanation: A formal statement given by a witness, typically in a legal proceeding, to establish facts about an event.

examples.japanese: {証人|しょうにん}が{法廷|ほうてい}で{証言|しょうげん}した。
{彼|かれ}の{証言|しょうげん}は{事件|じけん}の{解決|かいけつ}に{役立|やくだ}った。
examples.english: His testimony was helpful in solving the case.

examples.japanese: {目撃者|もくげきしゃ}の{証言|しょうげん}によると、{事故|じこ}は{深夜|しんや}に{起|お}きたらしい。
examples.english: According to the eyewitness testimony, the accident apparently occurred late at night.

notes:
USAGE:
{証言|しょうげん} is used both as a noun (testimony) and as a suru-verb ({証言|しょうげん}する = to testify). While most commonly used in legal contexts, it can also appear in journalism and historical accounts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {証言|しょうげん}する (to testify)
- {証言|しょうげん}を{得|え}る (to obtain testimony)
- {証言|しょうげん}{台|だい} (witness stand)
- {偽証|ぎしょう} (perjury — false testimony)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {証言|しょうげん}: spoken testimony by a witness
- {証拠|しょうこ}: physical evidence or proof
